title: SIEM Knowledge Engineer
description: At Securonix, we’re on a mission to secure the world by staying ahead of cyber threats, reinforcing all layers of our platform with AI capabilities. Our Securonix Unified Defense SIEM provides organizations with the first and only AI-Reinforced solution built with a cybersecurity mesh architecture on a highly scalable data cloud. Enhanced by Securonix EON ’s AI capabilities, our innovative cloud-native solution delivers a seamless CyberOps experience, empowering organizations to scale their security operations and keep up with evolving threats. Recognized as a five-time leader in the Gartner Magic Quadrant for SIEM and highly rated on Gartner Peer Insights , our award-winning Unified Defense SIEM provides organizations with 365 days of ‘hot’ data for rapid search and investigation, threat content-as-a-service, proactive defense through continuous peer and partner collaboration, and a fully integrated Threat Detection, Investigation, and Response (TDIR) experience—all within a single platform. Built on a cloud-native architecture, the platform leverages the Snowflake Data Cloud for unparalleled scalability and performance. At Securonix, we are driven by our core values and place our people at the heart of everything we do: Winning as One Team: We work together with universal respect to achieve aligned outcomes. Customer-Driven Innovation: We innovate to stay ahead of the market and create value for our customers. Agility in Action: We embrace change and are unified in our purpose and objectives amidst change. Join us as we redefine cybersecurity, innovate fearlessly, and grow together as one team. Role Summary: We are seeking a skilled technical communicator with expertise in cybersecurity, SIEM software, and related technologies. In this role, you will serve as a critical bridge between development teams in India and documentation teams in the US, ensuring the delivery of clear, accurate, and user-focused product content. Key Responsibilities: Develop a deep understanding of Securonix products , features, and enhancements. Test and validate new functionality to ensure documentation accuracy and completeness. Leverage the latest AI-driven tools to create, refine, and streamline technical content. Collaborate closely with developers and staff writers to produce comprehensive, user-friendly documentation . Create content that empowers customers to effectively deploy, manage, and succeed with our solutions. This is an opportunity to combine your technical expertise and communication skills to shape how customers interact with cutting-edge cybersecurity products. What You’ll Do & Achieve: Translate highly technical and complex cybersecurity concepts into clear, concise, and accessible content for diverse audiences. Leverage AI tools (such as GPT) to automatically generate documentation content from technical sources—including design documents, transcripts, product specifications, code, and development tickets. Test product features under development and provide feedback on software usability, ensuring a positive user experience. Review and refine documentation to ensure technical accuracy, clarity, and consistency. Identify gaps in existing documentation and propose improvements based on user feedback and technical insights. Minimum Qualifications: 3+ years of experience as a Threat Intelligence Analyst, Security Operations Center (SOC) Analyst, Security Engineer, Threat Hunter, or related cybersecurity role. Proven hands-on experience with SIEM software, ideally Securonix SNYPR or Unified Defense SIEM (UDS), or tools such as Splunk, QRadar, ArcSight, or Sentinel. Experience creating and using AI prompts to generate quality technical content. Proactive and self-motivated to seek information from various SMEs. Strong attention to detail. Comfortable working in a fast-paced, ever-changing environment. Proven ability to learn and master new products, tools, and technologies.

title: IAM Quality Analyst
description: Main Accountabilities · Own the QA and testing workstream for IAM CI backlog items, from test planning through production validation and closure. · Review intake requests, business requirements, solution designs, acceptance criteria, and technical specifications to identify test scope, dependencies, risks, and coverage gaps. · Develop and maintain test strategies, test plans, test scenarios, test cases, test data, traceability, and execution schedules for functional, integration, regression, security, and negative testing. · Execute SIT and coordinate UAT for IAM changes, integrations, access requests, provisioning and deprovisioning flows, access certifications, role or entitlement changes, and privileged access use cases. · Validate that solutions meet business requirements, IAM control expectations, enterprise security standards, regulatory obligations, and user needs. · Log, prioritise, track, retest, and close defects in JIRA, ensuring clear reproduction steps, expected results, supporting evidence, ownership, and timely escalation. · Coordinate with developers, business analysts, IAM Operations, product owners, application teams, and business testers to resolve issues and keep testing aligned with release timelines. · Provide concise status updates during daily stand-ups, project meetings, defect triage sessions, and release-readiness reviews, highlighting progress, risks, blockers, decisions, and required actions. · Support go-live readiness by confirming test completion, critical-defect closure, evidence availability, stakeholder solutions to business-as-usual support teams. · Maintain accurate QA documentation, test metrics, dashboards, audit evidence, lessons learned, and reusable regression packs across the assignment. · description: About Trellix Trellix is a global cybersecurity leader helping organizations build cyber resilience for the AI era. Combining AI-native security, operational threat intelligence, and automated detection and response, Trellix provides defense-grade protection at machine speed across on-premises, air-gapped, operational technology, hybrid, and cloud environments. Trellix helps customers anticipate threats, scale effective security operations, maintain business continuity, and adapt their security posture for the modern threat landscape. Working with a broad partner ecosystem and global intelligence collaborators, Trellix helps strengthen the collective defense against cybercriminals and state-sponsored attacks. At Trellix, we empower professionals at all career stages to expand their technical expertise, lead strategic initiatives, and make a tangible global impact. Whether you are an industry pioneer or an emerging specialist, Trellix provides the tools and opportunities to enhance and expand your skill set. Join our mission to scale AI-driven cyber defense alongside an AI-accelerated threat landscape, and help build a safer, more resilient future. More at https://trellix.com. Role Overview: The SOC Cloud Security Operations Analyst (Tier II) serves as an escalation point within the Security Operations Center (SOC) and overall Fusion Center. This role is responsible for monitoring, investigating, and remediating complex security alerts, conducting detailed technical analysis, and collaborating across different environments to mitigate threats. The ideal candidate pairs traditional SOC triage expertise with modern working knowledge of Security AI/ML tools and deep hands-on expertise in multi-cloud infrastructure security across AWS, Google Cloud Platform (GCP), Microsoft Azure, and Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) About the Role : Incident Investigation & Escalation: Take full ownership of security incidents; validate findings, determine scope and impact, execute remediation, and drive root cause analysis. Multi-Cloud Security Operations: Monitor, investigate, and contain threats across hybrid and multi-cloud infrastructure environments (AWS, GCP, Azure, OCI), utilizing native cloud security controls and centralized cloud security telemetry. AI-Enabled Threat Analysis: Leverage AI/ML-driven threat detection platforms, automated investigation tools, and LLM-assisted workflows to accelerate threat hunting, alert summarization, and query generation. Forensics & Malware Analysis: Perform technical triage, dynamic malware analysis, memory/artifact collection, and detailed log analysis across endpoint, network, and cloud telemetry. Vulnerability & Threat Management: Work in concert with Security Engineering and Product Security to prioritize and remediate active exploits, misconfigurations, and vulnerabilities. Global Handoffs & Mentorship: Lead seamless shift handoffs to global counterpart teams and provide ongoing mentoring and knowledge transfer Incident Documentation & Reporting: Author comprehensive incident reports, operational briefs, post-incident reviews, and tickets while ensuring evidence integrity for Incident Response workflows. About You : 1-2 years of direct operational security experience within an enterprise Security Operations Center (SOC) or Incident Response team acting as an escalation point (Tier II). Proven track record of handling high-severity incidents across both on-premises and enterprise multi-cloud environments. Cloud Security Infrastructure Expertise (AWS, GCP, Azure, OCI) AWS Security: Hands-on experience investigating alerts from AWS Security Hub, Amazon GuardDuty, AWS CloudTrail, VPC Flow Logs, and IAM Policy/Permission boundaries. Microsoft Azure Security: Experience with Azure Sentinel, Microsoft Defender for Cloud, Azure Activity Logs, NSGs, and Entra ID (Azure AD) identity threat detection. Google Cloud (GCP) Security: Familiarity with GCP Security Command Center (SCC), Cloud Audit Logs, VPC Firewall rules, and IAM conditional bindings. Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI) Security: Working knowledge of OCI Guardrail/Data Safe, OCI Audit Logs, Identity Domains, and OCI Network Security Groups (NSGs). Cloud Detection & Response (CDR): Solid understanding of cloud-native attack vectors (e.g., IAM credential abuse, metadata service exploitation, container escape, storage bucket misconfigurations, cross-cloud lateral movement). Artificial Intelligence & Operational AI Knowledge Working-Level Security AI Skills: Practical experience utilizing AI/ML-driven security tools (e.g., Security Copilot, AI-assisted EDR/SIEM features, automated triage playbooks). Prompt Engineering & Tooling: Ability to write effective natural language prompts to query security telemetry, generate KQL/SPL search strings, summarize complex threat reports, or analyze malicious scripts/code snippets. AI Risk Awareness: Basic understanding of security risks unique to AI integration (e.g., prompt injection, data leakage via LLMs, adversarial machine learning concepts). Core SOC & Technical Competencies Endpoint & Malware Analysis: Hands-on experience with enterprise EDR/XDR technology stacks (e.g., McAfee/Trellix, CrowdStrike, Defender for Endpoint) and dynamic malware analysis techniques. Network & OS Fundamentals: Deep technical understanding of OSI Model, TCP/IP, DNS, HTTP/S, SMTP, routing, and deep OS internals across Windows, Linux/Unix, and macOS. SIEM & Log Analysis: Expertise in querying and correlating enterprise SIEM telemetry, identifying pattern anomalies, and reducing false positives. Incident Handling Procedures: Demonstrated success executing NIST SP 800-61 / MITRE ATT&CK framework mapping during active containment and recovery phases. Soft Skills & Professional Attributes High-Pressure Execution: Proven ability to manage and prioritize multiple high-priority incidents under tight timelines. Strong Collaboration: Excellent written and verbal communication skills; adept at presenting complex technical findings to both technical peers and non-technical stakeholders. Global Team Alignment: High initiative with a collaborative style suitable for cross-functional and globally distributed teams. title: Cyber Incident Response - Director - Cybersecurity Operations
description: Cyber Data Risk and Resilience (CDRR) is part of the Global Technology organization and manages technology related risks on behalf of the Firm. CDRR's mandate is to enable the Firm to manage its technology and data related risks through implementing proactive, comprehensive and consistent risk management practices across the Firm to protect the franchise while capturing business opportunities. Morgan Stanley is looking for experienced security professionals to join the Firm's Cyber Incident Response Team (CIRT) as a Cyber Incident Response Analyst. The global CIRT provides a 24/7 first point of contact for security related incidents within the firm. Its members monitor the Firm's environment for abnormal behaviour and potential security breaches. Analysts review, triage, and investigate security alerts, and respond to or escalate security incidents. What you'll do in the role: Investigate cyber security incidents and threats. Interact with stakeholders and leadership teams as part of the response and remediation efforts. Improve the detection, escalation, containment and resolution of incidents. Enhance existing incident response methods, tools, and processes. Maintain knowledge of technologies and the threat landscape. Assist during non-core business hours during an emergency, critical or large-scale incident. Secondary Responsibilities VM Liaison Act as CIRT's primary point of contact with the Vulnerability Management team and engage with them on a regular basis. Maintain a current understanding of the status of vulnerabilities across the organization and be ready to lead or support investigations related to vulnerability exploitation. Translate vulnerability intelligence into actionable guidance for CIRT detection and response. Attack Surface Management Perform continuous discovery and mapping of the Firm's internal and external attack surface, including assets, services, domains, and cloud resources. Conduct vulnerability and exposure testing to identify misconfigurations, exposed services, and weaknesses. Feed attack surface insights into incident investigations and threat detection. What you'll bring to the role: Candidates should have a genuine interest in cyber security and a good understanding of the tactics, techniques and procedures of attackers. This role requires a detail oriented, critical thinker who can anticipate issues and solve problems. Candidates should be able to analyze large datasets to detect underlying patterns and drive to a root cause analysis. 5+ years of experience (or equivalent) with Security Analysis and Incident Response (i.e. working in SOC/CIRT/CSIRT/CERT). Understand the concept of a threat across multiple technologies and think like an adversary. Sound understanding of TCP/IP and networking concepts; security alerts and incidents. Excellent writing and presentation skills are required in order to communicate findings and recommendations. Experience with investigating common types of attacks; network packet analysis; log analysis and reviewing security events. Experience applying Open Source Intelligence (OSINT) techniques in support of investigations. Knowledge on Windows processes and Active Directory. Able to work on extended working hours during incidents. Hands-on experience with vulnerability management processes, vulnerability research, and assessing vulnerability impact on enterprise systems. Hands-on experience in Attack Surface Management, including continuous discovery and mapping, vulnerability and exposure testing, and risk prioritization and triage. Desired Skills: Experience investigating AI-assisted attacks is an advantage. Experience using AI to automate work or investigations is an advantage. Subject matter expert in one or multiple areas such as Windows, Unix, anti-virus, firewalls, intrusion detection, network and host based forensics. Scripting (Python, BASH, Perl, or PowerShell), coding or other development experience. In-depth knowledge of security event management, network security monitoring, log collection, and correlation. Experience in Splunk or Elastic usage or administration. Experience in Security Orchestration and Automated Response (SOAR) usage. Industry certifications: Incident Response: GCIH, GNFA, GREM or other related SANS certifications. Cloud security certifications (e.g., AWS, Azure, GCP security certifications, CCSP) are good to have. Vulnerability Management or Attack Surface Management related certifications are good to have. Experience in the financial industry. Understanding of Cloud Security. Knowledge on OWASP Top 10. WHAT YOU CAN EXPECT FROM MORGAN STANLEY: At Morgan Stanley, we raise, manage and allocate capital for our clients – helping them reach their goals. We do it in a way that’s differentiated – and we’ve done that for 90 years. Our values - putting clients first, doing the right thing, leading with exceptional ideas, committing to diversity and inclusion, and giving back - aren’t just beliefs, they guide the decisions we make every day to do what's best for our clients, communities and more than 80,000 employees in 1,200 offices across 42 countries. At Morgan Stanley, you’ll find an opportunity to work alongside the best and the brightest, in an environment where you are supported and empowered. Our teams are relentless collaborators and creative thinkers, fueled by their diverse backgrounds and experiences. We are proud to support our employees and their families at every point along their work-life journey, offering some of the most attractive and comprehensive employee benefits and perks in the industry. There’s also ample opportunity to move about the business for those who show passion and grit in their work. To learn more about our offices across the globe, please copy and paste https://www.morganstanley.com/about-us/global-offices into your browser. Morgan Stanley is an equal opportunity employer committed to building and maintaining a workforce that is diverse in experience and background. Our recruiting efforts reflect our strong commitment to a culture of inclusion, where individuals are hired, developed, and advanced based on their skills and talents. Our workforce reflects a broad cross-section of the global communities in which we operate, bringing a variety of backgrounds, talents, perspectives, and experiences. For more information, please visit: https://www.morganstanley.com/people-opportunities/eeo .

Investigate, document, and report on information security issues and emerging trends. Incident Response - reporting of cyber security incidents, mitigation advisement, quality review and after action. Use SOC monitoring tools and have a working understanding of systems. Such as SIEM systems, Intrusion Detection System, Data Loss Prevention, Antivirus System, to review and analyze pre-defined events. description: Join OneAdvanced: We are seeking an experienced Senior Cybersecurity GRC Analyst to be responsible for cybersecurity risk assessment across OneAdvanced. The role reports to the Head of Cybersecurity Risk and Controls. You will carry out risk assessments, evaluate security controls and evidence, maintain the risk register, and report on risk and remediation progress. You will work with security, technology and business teams on cybersecurity risks. What You Will Do: Cybersecurity Risk Assessment & Management: Carry out cybersecurity risk assessments across applications, infrastructure, cloud services, technology processes and security operations. Identify threats, vulnerabilities and control gaps, and assess their likelihood and impact. Assess inherent and residual risk, taking into account the design and effectiveness of existing controls. Document risk statements, evidence and findings, and recommend treatment. Agree treatment plans with risk owners: mitigation, acceptance, transfer or avoidance. Risk Register & Lifecycle Management: Maintain the cyber risk register, including owners, ratings, treatment decisions, actions and review dates. Track remediation, validate progress and escalate overdue or material risks. Reassess risks when threats, systems, business exposure or controls change. Assess risk acceptance and security exception requests and make a recommendation. Security Control Assessment & Assurance: Evaluate security controls and evidence against internal policies and industry frameworks. Assess controls in areas such as identity and access management, vulnerability management, cloud and application security, incident response, resilience and data protection. Apply NIST CSF 2.0, CIS Controls, ISO/IEC 27001:2022 when assessing control gaps. Work with control owners on remediation and keep the supporting documentation. Risk Governance, Monitoring & Reporting: Prepare risk reports, dashboards and management updates on exposure, trends, exceptions and remediation progress. Provide input to cybersecurity risk reviews and governance forums. Monitor key risk indicators and flag emerging or changing exposures. Keep cyber risk records in line with enterprise risk management processes and internal methodology. Continuous Improvement & Process Enhancement: Improve risk assessment templates, scoring, control mapping and reporting. Use automation or AI tools where they help with evidence review, analysis and reporting. Contribute to the cyber risk methodology and control library. Collaboration & Stakeholder Engagement: Work with security operations, engineering, application security, infrastructure, technology and business teams. Explain technical risks and treatment options to technical and non-technical stakeholders. What You Will Have: Skills and Experience: Minimum of 5 years in cybersecurity, including at least 4 years of hands-on cybersecurity risk management. Experience personally carrying out risk assessments, evaluating control gaps, documenting risk and tracking remediation, beyond audit or compliance coordination. Experience maintaining risk registers and managing risks through their lifecycle. Working knowledge of NIST CSF, CIS Controls, ISO/IEC 27001:2022 and SOC 2, applied in risk assessments and gap analysis. Technical understanding of identity and access management, vulnerability management, network, cloud and application security, incident response and resilience. Experience assessing inherent and residual risk and reviewing control evidence. Ability to turn technical findings into business risk and produce clear management reports. Strong analytical, documentation and communication skills, with the ability to manage competing priorities with limited supervision. Preferred Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree in Cybersecurity, Information Security, IT, Risk Management or equivalent experience. CRISC, CISA, CISSP or ISO 27001 Lead Auditor/Implementer. Exposure to third-party or supplier cybersecurity risk, including due diligence, assurance review and tracking remediation. Experience with GRC platforms, risk and reporting tools, or AI and automation tools. Behavioural Attributes: Practical, risk-based judgement, and willing to challenge assumptions.
